opportunities.title: Bid-intake and estimate-assembly agent for heavy civil pursuits
opportunities.problem: Crisdel is adding estimating capacity rather than freeing it: a Chief Estimator plus two Estimator (Civil / Heavy-Highway) requisitions are open across NJ and a new Virginia market, while the firm's own internship posting shows the bid workload itself (uploading drawings to Procore, distributing bid documents, collecting subcontractor pricing, quantity takeoffs, drafting RFIs and submittals) is still done by hand. Three simultaneous estimating seats in two regions, plus a third geography starting up, points to bid volume outpacing headcount, and each of the nine-plus agency prequalifications (FDOT, NJDOT, NJ Transit, Turnpike, NYSDOT, NYSTA, PennDOT, PTC, PANYNJ) adds its own bid forms and deadlines. (Estimating bottleneck is an inference from the requisition pattern, flagged as such in the profile.)
evidence: Chief Estimator plus two Estimator (Civil, Heavy/Highway) openings listed simultaneously in NJ and VA — https://jobs.localjobnetwork.com/s/e-CRISDEL-GROUP-INC-jobs-e119509.html?pbid=68438

Internship posting describes manual bid support: drawing uploads to Procore, bid document distribution, collecting subcontractor pricing, quantity takeoffs in AGTEK, RFI and submittal drafting — https://www.crisdel.com/summer-2027-internship/

Prequalified with FDOT, NJDOT, NJ Transit, NJ Turnpike Authority, NYSDOT, NY Thruway Authority, PennDOT, PA Turnpike Commission and PANYNJ, i.e. nine separate bid/submittal rulebooks — https://www.crisdel.com/company-overview/

New operating area in Ashburn/Sterling/Northern Virginia with a Project Engineer, two PMs, superintendents, an estimator and pipe/concrete foremen posted together — https://jobs.localjobnetwork.com/s/e-CRISDEL-GROUP-INC-jobs-e119509.html?pbid=68438

Vendor-reported benchmark: AI-assisted pre-takeoff saved ~6 hours per estimator per month and estimate comparison fell from 60 to 10 minutes (83% faster) across 4,000+ US contractors — self-reported product telemetry, no control group, treat as directional only — https://www.trimble.com/en/blog/construction/article/actual-results-mep-estimators-ai-assisted-takeoff
opportunities.agent_design: Trigger: a bid invitation, addendum or plan-set drop arriving at the estimating shared mailbox or a Procore bid folder. The agent extracts the scope summary, CSI divisions, key dates, bonding and insurance limits, DBE/SBE goals and the referenced wage determination; opens a bid workspace with a checklist per agency; builds the subcontractor invite list by trade from past award and quote history; sends scoped quote requests, chases non-responders on a schedule; ingests returned quotes into a leveling sheet with normalized unit prices, inclusion/exclusion flags and gap warnings; and produces an RFI list from drawing/spec conflicts plus an addenda-impact note. Systems touched: email/Outlook, Procore bid management, AGTEK exports, the estimating workbook. Human approval points: the estimator signs off the scope summary and shortlist before any quote request goes out, and every number that reaches a bid is approved by a named estimator — the agent never submits a price.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: It has to read plan sets and specs across PDF/CAD and AGTEK outputs, live inside Procore bid folders, hold state across a multi-week pursuit, and chase third parties on a schedule with a follow-up trail — none of which a chat subscription does. Outputs must be source-linked and defensible enough for an estimator to stake a bid on, and unit-price build-ups plus subcontractor quotes are commercially sensitive, so it needs a private or contractually constrained deployment rather than a consumer model.

impact_estimate.range: ~20-40 estimator hours per month recovered on bid prep and quote chasing, worth roughly $10k-$30k per year of estimator time, plus capacity to carry roughly one extra bid package per quarter per region without a new hire (avoided cost of an incremental estimator at the NJ median of $80,570)
impact_estimate.assumptions: 3-person estimating team (Chief + 2); 6-10 hours recovered per estimator per month, anchored to the Trimble vendor figure but discounted to the low end because that claim is self-reported telemetry with no control group; NJ Cost Estimator median $80,570 (~$39/hr unloaded), loaded at ~1.25x; excludes any win-rate, change-order or margin effect, which is not measured anywhere in the evidence base

opportunities.pilot_scope: One live NJDOT or NJ Turnpike bid package end to end in 3-4 weeks: document intake and scope/date/bond extractor, agency-specific checklist, subcontractor shortlist and automated quote chase, a quote leveling sheet, and an auto-generated RFI list — measured against the estimator's manual baseline on the same package.

opportunities.title: Weekly certified-payroll and prequalification compliance agent
opportunities.problem: Essentially all of Crisdel's work is public-works, which means a recurring weekly obligation: certified payroll records filed online through NJ Wage Hub and in hard copy to the contracting public body, PWCR certificates held for every named subcontractor, and ISNetworld safety/compliance evidence kept current per project. The firm is meeting this by adding people, not systems — it has posted a Construction Accounting & Compliance Administrator to support both the project-management and accounting teams, and its single HR administrator already carries FMLA, ACA/1095 and 401k reporting. Weekly, rules-based document assembly with hard deadlines is being absorbed by headcount. (That compliance load is documentation-heavy rather than strategic is an inference from the scoping of the new role and the HR administrator's listed duties.)
evidence: Construction Accounting & Compliance Administrator opening in South Plainfield, scoped to support both the project-management and accounting teams — https://jobs.localjobnetwork.com/s/e-CRISDEL-GROUP-INC-jobs-e119509.html?pbid=68438

ISNetworld is the firm's contractor safety/compliance platform and is marketed as an approved-contractor credential, i.e. ongoing evidence upkeep per project — https://www.crisdel.com/company-overview/
HR administrator handles onboarding, benefits, FMLA, ACA/1095 and 401k reporting in addition to recruiting for 49 open requisitions — https://www.crisdel.com/management-team/

Industry constraint: NJ Prevailing Wage Act requires weekly certified payroll submission, and as of Aug 15 2024 filing is required both through the NJ Wage Hub portal and in hard copy to the public body; records land in a searchable statewide database with some fields redacted — https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-3051.00 (O*NET task list for Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks, the occupation that owns this work)
opportunities.agent_design: Weekly trigger (end of pay week): pull timecards from timekeeping or the field Excel sheets, reconcile craft classifications and wage rates against the applicable wage determination and fringe schedule, flag apprentice-ratio and classification mismatches, then assemble the certified payroll record set and produce a filing-ready package for NJ Wage Hub plus a redaction-safe export for the public-body hard copy. In parallel it maintains a per-project compliance vault — subcontractor PWCR certificates, ISNetworld status, insurance certificates, expiry dates — auto-requesting renewals 30 days out and blocking a filing with a named-sub exception list. Systems touched: timekeeping/payroll, job cost, the Wage Hub filing workflow, ISNetworld records, a document store. Human approval: the accounting/compliance administrator reviews the exception report and approves every weekly filing and every classification correction; the agent never submits unapproved records.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: These records contain SSNs, I-9 data and union deduction detail and end up in a public, searchable state database, so this needs tenant-controlled/private deployment with retention and redaction logic, not a browser chatbot. It must reconcile timekeeping, job cost and the state portal, run on a weekly schedule it cannot miss, and leave an audit trail a public owner or NJDOL can inspect. Off-the-shelf payroll tools do payroll; they do not do multi-agency prevailing-wage filing prep plus subcontractor prequal tracking across nine agencies.

impact_estimate.range: ~15-25 hours per week of payroll/compliance admin reduced by 40-60%, i.e. roughly $12k-$25k per year of clerical time, plus reduced penalty and rejection exposure (a first PWCR-registration violation alone carries a penalty up to $2,500, and a rejected filing can stall payment on a public job)
impact_estimate.assumptions: 10-20 hours/week of payroll-clerk-level effort (lower band assumed because actual payroll volume is not disclosed); 40-60% reduction with a human still approving each filing; NJ Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks median $60,750 (~$29/hr); 52-week year; the 52-week cycle is assumed to continue for the whole portfolio, which the NJ Wage Hub mandate supports but which is not verified contract by contract

opportunities.pilot_scope: In 2-3 weeks: run one public-works project's certified payroll cycle twice — build the wage-determination matcher and exception report, generate a filing-ready NJ Wage Hub package and redaction-safe hard copy, and stand up the subcontractor document/expiry tracker with automated renewal requests. Compare against the prior two manual cycles.

opportunities.title: After-hours emergency response intake and dispatch agent
opportunities.problem: Crisdel publishes a 24/7 on-call emergency repair service with an Emergency Response Team promised to arrive 'within hours' at airports, bridges, ports, rail, roads and tunnels — but the only intake channels on the site are two office phone numbers, two fax numbers and a static Contact Form 7 form that captures name, email, phone, a state dropdown and free text. There is no project type, asset, location, severity or document field, no acknowledgement, no routing and no published after-hours number, so a 2am call about a closed runway lane most likely lands in voicemail with nobody triaging it. The form's missing fields also mean every inbound inquiry gets manually re-qualified by phone. (That after-hours handling is a weak point is an inference from the published 24/7 promise versus the published intake channels.)
evidence: Emergency repair services marketed as available on-call 24/7, with a team arriving within hours for airports, bridges, ports, rail, roads and tunnels — https://www.crisdel.com/emergency-repair-services/

Contact page offers only HQ phone/fax, Tampa phone/fax and a web form with name, email, phone, state dropdown and free text — no project type, severity, budget, schedule or file upload — https://www.crisdel.com/contact-us/
No live chat, chatbot or scheduling widget observed and no published business hours, so after-hours coverage rests entirely on phone pickup — https://www.crisdel.com/contact-us/

Two-office, multi-state footprint (South Plainfield NJ, Tampa FL) serving NJ, NY, PA, FL plus a new Virginia market, so dispatch has to find the right regional crew fast — https://www.crisdel.com/contact-us/; https://jobs.localjobnetwork.com/s/e-CRISDEL-GROUP-INC-jobs-e119509.html?pbid=68438
opportunities.agent_design: Triggers: any inbound call, voicemail transcript, web form, email or after-hours SMS. The agent transcribes and classifies the request (asset type, location/jurisdiction, severity, whether a lane or facility is closed), asks the caller the missing facts by SMS or email reply, identifies the owning agency or client and whether a contract or T&M basis applies, then checks the on-call roster and crew/equipment availability before paging the correct duty superintendent with a one-screen brief. It opens a ticket with a timestamped timeline, drafts the initial client acknowledgement and the later T&M ticket, and escalates again if the superintendent does not acknowledge within a set window. Audit points: duty superintendent accepts or overrides the dispatch; any pricing, commitment or agency notification requires manager approval. Delivered with a small dispatch console/dashboard (capability D work) so the office can see live callouts, response times and open tickets across NJ and FL.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This spans telephony, voicemail transcription, SMS and on-call paging with guaranteed escalation and a defensible response-time record — a chatbot on the website covers none of it. It must read roster and equipment availability from systems that were never built to talk to each other, and a silent drop carries liability on a public-owner emergency contract. Reliability, not conversation quality, is the product.

impact_estimate.range: ~2-5 hours per week of superintendent/PM time currently lost to triage, callbacks and re-qualifying callers, worth roughly $5k-$13k per year, plus unquantified protection against a missed or late emergency callout and against response-time commitments that public owners may score
impact_estimate.assumptions: 3 hours/week baseline of supervisor-level involvement, assumed because actual after-hours call volume is not disclosed anywhere; NJ First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades median $105,510 (~$51/hr), loaded at ~1.25x; no revenue figure is claimed because emergency/T&M volume is not published — the revenue side is deliberately left unquantified

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3 weeks on the HQ and Tampa lines in shadow mode: after-hours intake agent across form, email and voicemail, severity/location classifier, on-call paging with escalation, and a live callout dashboard with response-time logging. Week 1 runs beside the existing process; weeks 2-3 take live after-hours calls with the duty superintendent confirming every dispatch.

lead_score.rationale: Pain 22/30: the strain is documented rather than described — three open estimating requisitions across two regions plus a third market starting up, a brand-new accounting-and-compliance seat bolted onto an already-loaded single HR administrator, and a published 24/7 emergency promise with no intake layer behind it. Points are withheld because no owner or manager is quoted anywhere saying this hurts, and customer/employee reviews were unavailable (Indeed, Glassdoor, BBB, Yelp all blocked), so there is no external corroboration. Fit 17/20: all three opportunities are core capability-A work built on systems Crisdel already runs (Procore, AGTEK, ISNetworld, Topcon, WordPress/Contact Form 7), and the firm publicly markets technology adoption, which shortens the sales cycle. Ability to pay 14/20: a 1968-founded family-owned heavy civil contractor prequalified with nine agencies and carrying an $81M project can fund this, but headcount and revenue are unpublished and could not be verified, so the score stays moderate. Ease 10/15: the estimating and certified-payroll pilots are cleanly scoped on a single bid or project, but the two-office multi-state structure, email-based resume intake (no ATS) and unverified internal IT make data access the main pilot risk. Strategic 13/15: NJ prevailing-wage certified payroll and multi-agency prequalification are the same for every public-works contractor in the state, so the compliance agent is a repeatable product for a large local market; the estimating and emergency-dispatch patterns transfer to any heavy civil firm. Total 76.

best_evidence_signal: 49 advertised openings including a Chief Estimator plus two Estimators in NJ and VA, while the firm's own internship posting still describes manual takeoffs, phoning subcontractors for pricing and hand-drafted RFIs — https://jobs.localjobnetwork.com/s/e-CRISDEL-GROUP-INC-jobs-e119509.html?pbid=68438
